title: A bus a test run spawns is the run's
intention: A bus that a test run causes to start is the run's: its unit carries the run's CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID and collects itself when it fails, so the tester's stop takes it and no failed bus unit lingers.
why: Law 9 and Law 7 via the tester's charter (a run owns what it started, c64adc092835): a failed bus left by a run sits in the live user manager as a corpse nobody's stop reaches, which is noise at a diagnostic surface. Law 3: measured 2026-10-11 (8 corpses) and again 2026-10-18 by the new proof (a run's bus outlives the run, active).
traces_to: Law 9 and Law 7 via the tester's charter (a run owns what it started, c64adc092835): a failed bus left by a run sits in the live user manager as a corpse nobody's stop reaches, which is noise at a diagnostic surface. Law 3: measured 2026-10-11 (8 corpses) and again 2026-10-18 by the new proof (a run's bus outlives the run, active).
how: In cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py _spawn, after the fixed systemd-run argv and before '--', append --setenv=CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID=<id> and -p CollectMode=inactive-or-failed only when CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID is set in the caller's environment, which is the exact mark 2120e74dcf44 gave ensure_ground_loop. Outside a run the argv is unchanged. The proof cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_a_bus_a_test_run_spawns_is_the_runs.py calls ensure_bus from a unit beside the user manager. Measured 2026-10-18: 1 of 4 today, 4 of 4 with the change. Builder notes: Questions a Haiku builder would need, answered. (a) Only cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py changes, in _spawn. (b) In the argv list, end it after the StandardError line, i.e. drop the trailing ', "--", *cmd' from the literal. (c) Then add the three-line comment and: test_id = os.environ.get("CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID"); if test_id: argv += [f"--setenv=CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID={test_id}", "-p", "CollectMode=inactive-or-failed"]; then argv += ["--", *cmd]. (d) Copy the comment shape from cairn/tools/base/shim.py lines 157-159. (e) The proof is already written and committed; run it. Expect 1 of 4 before and 4 of 4 after.
falsifier: Falsifier: cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_a_bus_a_test_run_spawns_is_the_runs.py has four teeth. (1) The bus unit ensure_bus starts from a caller carrying CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID carries that id in the manager's Environment record. (2) Its CollectMode is inactive-or-failed. (3) A tester run whose subject starts a bus leaves no unit. (4) With no id the unit carries none and CollectMode stays inactive. Measured 2026-10-18 on today's remote.py: 1 of 4, teeth 1-3 red; with the change applied aside, 4 of 4. Every bus_client proof stays green. Horizon: PROVED, with the reverted remote.py redding teeth 1-3 in the hollow reading.
watchme: none, because the outcome is a structural property measured by cairn/tools/bus_client/proofs/test_a_bus_a_test_run_spawns_is_the_runs.py, which reruns at every bin/cairn test --seal touching remote.py; a recurrence would show as cairn-bus-* units in 'systemctl --user list-units --all cairn-bus-*' and as the live trouble a-bus-a-test-run-spawns-is-not-the-runs in the lane printed by bin/cmd/slate

The exact change to cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py, as a unified diff; apply it verbatim: @@ -162,8 +162,14 @@
             "--working-directory", str(_CLASS_ROOT),
             f"--setenv=HOME={env_home}", f"--setenv=PATH={os.environ.get('PATH', '')}",
             "-p", "SuccessExitStatus=3",
-            "-p", f"StandardOutput=append:{log}", "-p", f"StandardError=append:{log}",
-            "--", *cmd]
+            "-p", f"StandardOutput=append:{log}", "-p", f"StandardError=append:{log}"]
+    # inside a test run the bus is the run's (the twin of 2120e74dcf44's mark on the loop):
+    # systemd-run hands a unit the MANAGER's environment, so the run's id is carried by hand where
+    # the tester's stop reads it (the manager's record), and a failed bus of a run collects itself
+    test_id = os.environ.get("CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID")
+    if test_id:
+        argv += [f"--setenv=CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID={test_id}", "-p", "CollectMode=inactive-or-failed"]
+    argv += ["--", *cmd]
